name: DocVQA
description: DocVQA is a large scale dataset for Visual Question Answering (VQA) on document images. It consists of 50,000 questions defined on 12,767 document images sourced from the UCSF Industry Documents Library. The dataset covers a wide variety of document types including letters, forms, reports, tables, and more, spanning multiple industries and decades. Questions are categorized into 9 types based on reasoning requirements, making it suitable for analyzing model performance across different question types.
creator: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar
publisher: CVIT, IIIT Hyderabad, India and Computer Vision Center, UAB, Spain
citeAs: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar. DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images. arXiv:2007.00398v3 [cs.CV], 5 Jan 2021.
rai:dataCollection: Document images were sourced from the UCSF Industry Documents Library. Documents were downloaded from different collections and pages were hand-picked for use in the dataset. Majority of documents in the library are binarized; binarized images were minimized to avoid poor image quality being a bottleneck. Pages with tables, forms, lists and figures were prioritized over pages with only running text. Questions and answers were collected with the help of remote workers using a web-based annotation tool in a three-stage process.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, User-generated content data
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Document images sourced from the UCSF Industry Documents Library (https://www.industrydocuments.ucsf.edu/), covering 5 industries (tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel, chemical) from documents as early as 1900 to as recent as 2018.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Documents span from 1900 to 2018. Most documents are from the 1960-2000 period.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset is split randomly in an 80-10-10 ratio into train, validation, and test splits. The train split has 39,463 questions and 10,194 images; the validation split has 5,349 questions and 1,286 images; and the test split has 5,188 questions and 1,287 images.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Binarized images were minimized in the dataset. Pages with tables, forms, lists and figures were prioritized. Questions flagged as inapt due to language issues or ambiguity during stage 2 annotation were excluded from the dataset. OCR tokens were extracted using a commercial OCR application and serialized in top-left to bottom-right order for use in reading comprehension models.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotation was organized in three stages. Stage 1: Remote workers were shown a document image and asked to define at most 10 question-answer pairs. Workers were instructed to ask questions answerable using text in the image and to enter answers verbatim. Multiple ground truth answers per question were encouraged where warranted. Stage 2: A different worker was shown the image and questions (without stage 1 answers) and required to enter answers and assign one or more question types to each question. Workers could flag questions as inapt due to language issues or ambiguity. Stage 3: If no answers from stage 1 matched any answers from stage 2, the question was sent for review by the authors, who could edit questions and answers or add new answers before accepting or ignoring the question.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Web-based annotation tool (custom, screen grabs shown in appendix)
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: If none of the answers entered in stage 1 match exactly with any answers from stage 2, the question is sent for a third-stage review by the authors. Questions flagged as inapt in stage 2 are not included in the dataset. Multiple ground truth answers per question are allowed.
rai:annotationsPerItem: At most 10 question-answer pairs per document image; each question verified by at least two annotators across stages 1 and 2, with a third review by authors when answers mismatch.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Commercial OCR application (used for extracting OCR tokens from document images for baselines and upper bound computation).
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset, code and leaderboard are available at docvqa.org. No explicit versioning, update schedule, or deprecation policy is described in the paper.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains industry documents from the UCSF Industry Documents Library that may include names of people, institutions, and places as part of document content. Named entities such as names of people appear among the most frequent answers.
rai:dataSocialImpact: DocVQA aims to inspire a 'purpose-driven' approach in Document Analysis and Recognition (DAR) research by introducing a high-level task that dynamically drives DAR algorithms to conditionally interpret document images. This could drive methods that use low-level cues (text, layout, arrangements) and high-level goals (purpose, relationship, domain knowledge) in solving problems of practical importance.
rai:dataBiases: A large majority of questions start with 'what is the', asking for date, title, total, amount or name. There are questions repeatedly asked about dates, titles and page numbers. Many documents are from food and nutrition related collections due to availability of non-binarized images. Most documents are from the 1960-2000 period.
rai:dataLimitations: Majority of documents in the UCSF library are binarized, which negatively affects image quality; binarized images were minimized but not entirely excluded. OCR errors can result in incorrect answers even when models correctly ground questions. Models struggle with questions requiring understanding of figures, diagrams, photographs, and document structure/layout. The dataset is limited to English-language documents from 5 specific industries.
rai:dataUseCases: Training, Validation, and Testing of Visual Question Answering (VQA) models on document images. Benchmarking of reading comprehension and scene text VQA models. The dataset is intended to inspire purpose-driven document image analysis and recognition research. A leaderboard is available at docvqa.org for model comparison.
